strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, utility side from BAFU's own emulsion-polymerisation module, amounts calibrated within 0.5-2x of it
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The monomer is a mass balance (1 kg of PVC carries 1 kg of vinyl chloride; chain-growth polymerisation adds the monomer unchanged). The utility side - nitrogen blanketing, compressed air, process water, furnace gas, steam, electricity, auxiliary organics and the treatment of the unpolluted process water - is the input list of BAFU's own unit process 'Emulsion polymerisation, polyvinylchlorid' [RER], with its amounts as the centre of 0.5-2x bounds. Caveat, stated rather than hidden: that module is generic. Its one consumer in BAFU-2026 is 'Polyvinylalcohol, at plant' (1.94 kg of it), and its monomer slot is filled with 1.355 kg of dichloromethane, which is not a PVC reagent. Only its utility rows are used here; the monomer slot is replaced by vinyl chloride. That is why this is S3 with a template for the utilities, not S2.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: Polystyrene, expandable, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model from the dataset's own process description: styrene by mass balance, blowing agent and utilities calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory; what it says about EPS is an error correction (sec. 3.8, the rejected 28.5 kg of natural gas per kg). The input list here comes from the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, which for EPS is unusually explicit and names, in order: styrene monomer, organic peroxide initiators, an aqueous phase, flame retardant and elemental carbon, suspension stabilisers, chain transfer agents, expanding aids, nucleating agents, plasticisers, pentane as the blowing agent, heating to 80-150 C, a centrifuge, drying and sieving, and a coating step. Amounts for none of them are printed anywhere in the bundle, so styrene is fixed by mass balance and everything else is fitted. The flame retardant and the elemental carbon of grey EPS are left out on purpose: no dataset is named for either and proposing one would be guessing - see gaps in the comment.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (technology)
evidence.note: 'Expandable Polystyrene (EPS) is produced by polymerisation of styrene monomer, a chain-growth reaction which is mostly initiated by free radical organic initiators. ... Styrene charged with organic peroxide initiators is added to an aqueous phase and forms a suspension upon stirring. Flame retardant and elemental carbon, as well as auxiliaries such as suspension stabilisers, chain transfer agents, expanding aids, nucleating agents and plasticisers can also be added. The styrene droplets polymerise to polystyrene during heating of the reactor between 80 and 150 C. Blowing agent, typically pentane, is added to the reactor during polymerisation and dissolves in the polymer, producing the Expandable Polystyrene bead. After the reactor is cooled, the polymer is separated from the water phase using a centrifuge. The EPS beads are dried and sieved into the required size fractions before being coated with additive'

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: sec. 3.8 Obvious errors corrected in PE data
evidence.note: 'According to the latest PlasticsEurope data, methane emissions were first estimated for Polystyrene expandable seven times higher (0.226 kg vs. 0.031 kg) than previously estimated in UVEK 2025. This discrepancy is largely due to the significant consumption of natural gas - 28.5 kg - required to produce just 1 kg of polystyrene. Since such a high input is unrealistic a correction has been made.' A rejected figure, so it cannot be used as an amount; it is recorded because it is the only process-energy number the report ever prints for this dataset, and because it means the published vector for EPS carries a hand-made correction of unstated size.

nodes.name: Polystyrene, expandable, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polystyrene, expandable, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Suspension polymerisation of styrene with a pentane blowing agent, per kg of EPS beads. Gaps: the flame retardant, the elemental carbon of grey EPS (4 of the 14 plants behind the eco-profile), the peroxide initiator and the bead coating are named by the dataset and modelled only through the generic 'Chemicals organic, at plant'. Note also that the target carries 1.435 kg of 'Disposal, salt tailings potash mining, 0% water, to residual material landfill {CH}' per kg of EPS. Tab. 3.1 of the cited report (p. 11 of the PDF, the continuation page that pdftotext returns empty because the table is an image) shows where that comes from: 'tailings (deposited)', 'Overburden (deposited)' and 'Waste salt from KCl-production (wfr)' are all mapped to that one potash-tailings *treatment* dataset. Mining overburden routed through a waste-treatment chain is what gives the EPS target its three largest kilogram flows - 30.6 kg of waste water to river, 18.3 kg of air and 1.44 kg of basalt per kg of polystyrene - and it is why this dataset's kg-mass and top-50 scores cannot be met by any model of the polymerisation. Nothing in this model reproduces it, and nothing should. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

strategy.label: top-down model from the dataset's own process description: monomer by mass balance, utilities from the BAFU chemicals template and calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory for this dataset. The input list comes from the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, 'production by different types of polymerization out of MMA'. The field names the monomer outright; 'sheet' is the cast form. Chain-growth (addition) polymerisation: the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No conversion-loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the true value can only be higher - fixed, not fitted. Same convention as the committed HDPE / LDPE / LLDPE / PP / PVC specs. The monomer is itself an unflagged PlasticsEurope eco-profile (results/system_terminated_extended.csv, detected_by=structure), so this model terminates on an aggregated dataset and the structural check says so - correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together. The BAFU datasets for beads and for sheet carry the same technology text and differ only in their cumulative vectors, and nothing in the bundle says how the two forms differ in process, so the two specs differ only in what the fit puts into the free utilities. That is stated here rather than hidden.

replaces.name: Polypropylene, granulate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. 'Propylene, at plant [RER]' is not one of the 101, so the harness does not flag it, but it is not a transparent unit process either: it carries 8 technosphere exchanges, all of them waste-treatment services, and 143 elementary flows - the same APME/PlasticsEurope shape as the datasets being rebuilt here. The chain therefore still terminates on aggregated data one level down, and saying so is part of the result.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like propylene production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.'

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: Polypropylene 75.62 MJ/kg. Propylene is not one of the 14 datasets of the report, so Tab. 5.3 gives no monomer figure to subtract and there is no cross-check on the fitted process energy for this one. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polypropylene, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polypropylene, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve.

technosphere.comment: mass balance of chain-growth polymerisation: the repeat unit is the monomer, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer; no conversion-loss figure is printed in any report of the bundle, so this is a lower bound, fixed (not fitted)

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid
technosphere.comment: named by the dataset ('electricity ... production'), quantified nowhere in the bundle -> calibrated, unbounded
technosphere.supplier_name: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
technosphere.comment: named by the dataset ('steam production'), quantified nowhere in the bundle -> calibrated, unbounded
technosphere.supplier_name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

residual.note: Hybrid node: the explicit exchanges above plus these residual elementary flows, so that the cumulative inventory of the hybrid node equals the original BAFU system process exactly. The residual is what the explicit model does NOT yet explain.

replaces.name: Hydrogen cyanide, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft); the report's tables are literature data, the dataset itself is a cumulated inventory
strategy.note: basis: per kg of hydrogen cyanide, Tab. 43.2 / 43.3 / 43.4 of chapter 43 of ecoinvent report No. 8 (Althaus et al. 2007), all printed per kg or per kg in grams; allocation: None stated. The chapter reports three co-products per kg HCN - 0.23 kg hydrogen (BMA route, if not burnt), 0.34 kg ammonium sulfate sold as fertiliser and 0.02 kg sodium cyanide - but gives no allocation factor, so every burden below stays with the HCN.; 3 of 4 inputs carry a printed amount, 1 a printed range, 0 no number in the report. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 f7af81ba5953b5ff…

gaps_reported_by_model: Electricity: not mentioned anywhere in the excerpt, although the Andrussow reactor, the ammonia absorber and the HCN stripper all need it.
Process water and cooling water: not given ('Wastewater / Liquid wastes: No values available.').

Water emissions: the excerpt states outright that no values are available, yet the aggregated dataset carries water emissions; those necessarily come from the upstream chain in the cumulated original.

Infrastructure (chemical plant) and feedstock transport: not mentioned; ecoinvent's own convention for this family (4.0E-10 units of 'chemical plant, organics', 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor) is a BAFU template, not something this excerpt prints.

The Andrussow/BMA split: the excerpt says only 'BMA accounts for 15 % of the total European production', and Tab. 43.2/43.3/43.4 do not say which route each column belongs to except for Tab. 43.4 (BMA).
Oxygen / air for the Andrussow route (equation 1) is not quantified.
The catalyst (platinum gauze) is described qualitatively and never quantified.
skipped_items: Total process energy: ignore — Cross-check only, not a separate input: 31 MJ is the same energy as the natural-gas lines above (0.68 kg x 45.4 MJ/kg = 30.9 MJ). Counting it again would double the fuel.

Hydrogen: co-product — Co-product of the BMA route only, and only when not burnt in the process. The point estimate chosen for the fuel line above is the combustion route, in which this hydrogen is consumed internally, so it is recorded as a co-product but not credited.

Ammonium sulfate: co-product — Sold as fertiliser, so an economic co-product; the report gives no allocation factor, and none is applied here (all burdens stay with HCN). Note the report's own formula slip: ammonium sulfate is (NH4)2SO4, not Na2SO4.
Sodium cyanide: co-product — Listed under solid wastes; no allocation given.

nodes.name: Hydrogen cyanide, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Hydrogen cyanide, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 436-438

technosphere.comment: Tab. 43.2 'Resource consumption for the production of HCN (kg/kg)'; the feedstock of both the Andrussow and the BMA route (2 NH3 + 2 CH4 + 3 O2 -> 2 HCN + 6 H2O).

provenance.mapping_reason: The excerpt lists ammonia as a purchased precursor, not as something made on site, so the delivered form ('at regional storehouse') beats the two production routes ('steam reforming' / 'partial oxidation'), which would also force an arbitrary choice between them; this is also what BAFU's own 'Acrylonitrile from Sohio process, at plant' consumes (0.38774 kg of exactly this dataset).

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Natural gas, high pressure, at consumer
technosphere.comment: Tab. 43.2, the methane fed to the reactor (2 NH3 + 2 CH4 + 3 O2 -> 2 HCN + 6 H2O). Printed in kg; every natural-gas supply dataset in BAFU is in MJ, so the printed kg is converted with the standard heating value.
technosphere.supplier_name: Natural gas, high pressure, at consumer

provenance.factor_source: lower heating value of natural gas 45.4 MJ/kg (ecoinvent v2 convention); cross-checked against the same chapter's 'A total of 31 MJ is required per kg of HCN', which is 0.68 kg x 45.4 MJ/kg = 30.9 MJ
provenance.mapping_reason: The reactor feed is gas as delivered, not gas burnt, so the supply dataset is right rather than a furnace; RER beats CH and GLO because the target is a European average.

technosphere.comment: Tab. 43.2. Used to scrub the unreacted ammonia; consistent with the solid-waste line '0.34 kg of ammonium sulfate ... are produced per kg of HCN'.

provenance.mapping_reason: Generic concentrated sulphuric acid; the runner-up, 'Sulphuric acid from viscose production', is a by-product route from one specific industry and would import a viscose background the excerpt does not mention.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: Tab. 43.3 'Energy consumption for the production of HCN (kg/kg)' gives two columns, 'Hydrogen export route' 0.78 and 'Hydrogen combustion route' 0.51. The point estimate is the combustion route because Tab. 43.4's air emissions are stated to belong to it: 'These figures ... are calculated values based on the combustion of hydrogen gas in the process as a fuel that replaces part of the natural gas burned as a fuel.' The two columns are the printed range, so the amount is calibratable between them. Mapped to a heat-from-natural-gas dataset because BAFU has no 'natural gas burned' dataset in kg; the MJ of gas is charged as MJ of heat, which understates the gas by the furnace efficiency (~10 %). Flagged medium.
technosphere.supplier_name: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.factor_source: lower heating value of natural gas 45.4 MJ/kg (ecoinvent v2 convention; cross-check with the same chapter's 'A total of 31 MJ is required per kg of HCN', which equals 0.68 kg x 45.4 MJ/kg)
provenance.mapping_reason: Tab. 43.3 is gas burnt as process fuel, so a combustion dataset is needed. 'Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW' is the dataset every ecoinvent-v2 organic-chemical unit process in BAFU uses for exactly this (2.0 MJ of it appears in Cumene, Ethyl benzene, Bisphenol A, Phosgene and Aniline), which beats the near-identical 'Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW' on consistency with the family; 'xxx Heat ... low-NOx' is an xx-marked legacy dataset and 'District heat, at consumer' is the wrong delivery form.

biosphere.comment: Tab. 43.4 'Air emissions from the production of HCN (g/kg)', BMA process.

provenance.mapping_reason: 'Dust (SPM)' is a single unspeciated particulate figure; of the candidates only the particle flows are the right substance, and PM10 is the ecoinvent/EF convention for an unspeciated dust figure - it beats 'Particles (PM0.2)', which would claim a fineness the report does not state, and 'Particulates, unspecified' in bafu-2026-residual, which has no EF counterpart and would add a flow the target does not carry.

biosphere.comment: Tab. 43.4. Printed as SOx; mapped to sulfur dioxide, the ecoinvent/EF convention for SOx reported as a single figure.

provenance.mapping_reason: SOx reported as one figure is inventoried as SO2 in ecoinvent and EF 3.1, and the target's own vector carries Sulfur Dioxide, not Sulfur Oxides; the emissions-to-air compartment beats the soil and water entries of the same flow.
The methane comes from natural gas, so the fossil flow, not the biogenic one; 'Methanethiol' and 'Methanesulfonic Acid' are different substances that only match the search string.
NOx as a sum is the 'Nitrogen Oxides' flow; 'Nitrogen Dioxide' would claim a speciation the report does not give and 'Nitrogen' is the element.

biosphere.comment: Tab. 43.4 = 2.474 kg CO2 per kg HCN, against 4.69 kg in the cumulated vector of the same chapter, so about half the dataset's CO2 is direct - a plausible split for a fired reactor.

provenance.mapping_reason: Fossil carbon from natural gas; the biogenic and land-use-change variants are the wrong origin, and the 'Resources from air' entries are uptake, not release.

residual.note: Hybrid node: the explicit exchanges above plus these residual elementary flows, so that the cumulative inventory of the hybrid node equals the original BAFU system process exactly. The residual is what the explicit model does NOT yet explain.

datasets.bafu_name: Polystyrene, general purpose, GPPS, at plant

replaces.name: Polystyrene, general purpose, GPPS, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model from the dataset's own process description: monomer by mass balance, utilities from the BAFU chemicals template and calibrated
strategy.note:
NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory for this dataset. The input list comes from the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, 'polymerization out of ethylene and benzene by free radical processes'. The field describes the chain back to the cracker ('out of ethylene and benzene'), which is the route to styrene; the monomer of general-purpose polystyrene is styrene and nothing else. Chain-growth (addition) polymerisation: the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No conversion-loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the true value can only be higher - fixed, not fitted. Same convention as the committed HDPE / LDPE / LLDPE / PP / PVC specs. The monomer is itself an unflagged PlasticsEurope eco-profile (results/system_terminated_extended.csv, detected_by=structure), so this model terminates on an aggregated dataset and the structural check says so - correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together. 

AFTER THE FIT. All five utilities went to zero (electricity 5.5E-11 kWh, heat 6.9E-9 MJ, both transports ~1E-9 tkm, the plant 3.6E-21 units), so the node is exactly '1 kg of aggregated styrene' - which is what the evidence says and is the honest outcome. Its headline flows are close: fossil CO2 +29 %, methane -2 %, biogenic CO2 +7 %, SO2 -8 %, NOx -13 %, NMVOC -9 %. Its overall flow agreement is nevertheless 25 of 1667 (1 %), and the reason is not the chemistry: 'Styrene, at plant' declares 0.5615 kg of hazardous waste to incineration per kg, against 0.0070 kg for this dataset, 0.0088 for HIPS and 0.0022 for benzene. A polymer's cradle-to-gate profile cannot contain 80x less waste than the monomer it is made of, so one of the two numbers is wrong, and the mass balance of the rest of the family says it is the styrene one. Every flow that hazardous-waste chain feeds - calcite +1010 %, gravel +1120 %, rock salt +3094 %, chloride to water +4690 % - is that single exchange, not this model. See exports/README.md, 'The APME eco-profiles the type=2 flag missed'.

evidence.source: BAFU-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target
evidence.note: quoted in the strategy note; it is the structural evidence for the input list

evidence.source: locate step of the reverse-bafu route
evidence.note: specs/evidence/1235438d-3385-3bd1-8921-17951c10c464/response-0-locate.json - no report in the BAFU-2026 documentation bundle prints a unit-process inventory for this dataset. The cited report is only the 17-page front matter of ecoinvent report No. 11; all 114 bundled reports were converted with pdftotext and searched.

evidence.note: Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990.

evidence.source: BAFU-2026 itself, as a named template
evidence.where: Cumene / Ethyl benzene / Phosgene / Aniline, at plant [RER]
evidence.note: BAFU template, not a report figure. Every ecoinvent-v2 organic-chemical unit process in BAFU-2026 carries the same five-line utility block: 0.333 kWh of 'Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid', 2.0 MJ of 'Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW' [CH], 4.0E-10 units of 'Chemical plant, organics', and transport at 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kilogram of precursor. Verified exchange by exchange on Cumene, at plant (0.684 kg benzene + 0.369 kg propylene = 1.053 kg of precursor -> 0.632 tkm rail, 0.105 tkm lorry), Ethyl benzene, at plant (1.030 -> 0.619 / 0.103), Phosgene, liquid, at plant (1.040 -> 0.624 / 0.104) and Aniline, at plant (1.352 -> 0.814 / 0.136). That is the named template this amount comes from.

nodes.reference_product: Polystyrene, general purpose, GPPS, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step only, per kg of product, from 1 kg of styrene. The eight waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges are deliberately not part of this model - they were never collapsed away - following the committed PlasticsEurope specs. The consequence, measured in results/checks/, is that the target's cumulative vector gets a long tail of flows from those disposal chains that no model omitting them can reach.

technosphere.comment: Chain-growth (addition) polymerisation: the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No conversion-loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the true value can only be higher - fixed, not fitted. Same convention as the committed HDPE / LDPE / LLDPE / PP / PVC specs.

The dataset's ecoSpold technology field, 'product out of hydrogen cyanide and acetone', is the classic ACH route, and BAFU carries the intermediate as its own dataset ('xx Acetone cyanohydrin, at plant'), so the model is built one step at a time rather than collapsing the two: acetone + HCN -> ACH is the cyanohydrin spec, and this spec is the amidation/esterification step. C4H7NO (acetone cyanohydrin, 85.106) + H2SO4 (98.072) + CH3OH (methanol, 32.042) -> C5H8O2 (methyl methacrylate, 100.117) + NH4HSO4 (ammonium bisulfate, 115.103); mass balance 215.220 = 215.220. Per kg of MMA: 85.106/100.117 = 0.85006 kg of acetone cyanohydrin, 98.072/100.117 = 0.97957 kg of sulphuric acid and 32.042/100.117 = 0.32005 kg of methanol, with 1.14973 kg of ammonium bisulfate as co-product. Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990. Amounts fixed, not fitted. The ammonium bisulfate co-product weighs more than the product itself and nothing in the bundle gives an allocation or says whether the plant regenerates the acid, so no credit is taken and that is the single largest uncertainty in this spec. The acetone cyanohydrin input is itself an unflagged eco-profile (rebuilt here), so the structural check flags a dependency.

replaces.name: Nylon 66, glass-filled, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the two components the dataset's name and technology field state, split fitted under a 1 kg mass constraint
strategy.note:
NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field states the composition qualitatively - 'production out of hexamethylene diamine and adipic acid, filled with glass fibers' - and both components exist in BAFU: the unfilled polymer as an unflagged eco-profile and 'Glass fibre, at plant' [RER] as a real 20-input unit process. Compounding is a physical blend, so polymer + glass = 1.000 kg per kg of compound, which is imposed with mass_sum; the glass content is nowhere quantified in the bundle (commercial grades run 15-50 %), so the split is fitted, not measured, and is flagged low confidence. Note the circularity BAFU already contains and this spec inherits: 'Glass fibre, at plant' itself consumes 0.0283 kg of 'Nylon 6, at plant' as a sizing agent, so a glass-filled nylon depends on nylon twice.

AFTER THE FIT - READ THIS BEFORE USING THE AMOUNTS. The fit put 0.9995 kg on the polymer and 2.3E-4 kg on the glass fibre, i.e. it modelled a glass-*filled* compound as unfilled polymer; commercial grades carry 15-50 % glass. The inventory agreement it buys is real (601 of 1669 determined flows within +-10 % (36 %), 20 of the 50 largest kilogram flows, 89 % of the kilogram mass, median |delta| 12.2 %) and the node is a fair reconstruction of the target's flows, but its composition is not a statement about the product and must not be quoted. The mechanism is the same one recorded on the ABS, SAN and HIPS specs: under a mass constraint the fit empties whichever candidate is an ecoinvent unit process - here 'Glass fibre, at plant', a 20-input dataset that drags a full ~1670-flow background into a target whose eco-profile reports ~145 substances - and keeps the candidate that belongs to the same APME family and therefore shares the target's waste-treatment chains. No bound was moved after the score was seen.

replaces.name: Toluene diisocyanate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the three reagents the dataset names plus the nitric acid the equation requires, amounts from the three reaction equations with molar masses, utilities calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field names three reagents - 'production out of phosgene, toluene and hydrogen' - which is the toluene -> dinitrotoluene -> toluenediamine -> TDI route and nothing else; hydrogen is only ever used to reduce the nitro groups, so the field implies the nitration and therefore the nitric acid, which is added here for that reason and flagged. Three steps. Nitration: C7H8 (toluene, 92.141) + 2 HNO3 (126.024) -> C7H6N2O4 (dinitrotoluene, 182.135) + 2 H2O (36.030); 218.165 = 218.165. Hydrogenation: C7H6N2O4 + 6 H2 (12.096) -> C7H10N2 (toluenediamine, 122.171) + 4 H2O (72.060); 194.231 = 194.231. Phosgenation: C7H10N2 + 2 COCl2 (197.820) -> C9H6N2O2 (TDI, 174.159) + 4 HCl (145.832); 319.991 = 319.991. Per kg of TDI: 92.141/174.159 = 0.52906 kg toluene, 126.024/174.159 = 0.72361 kg HNO3, 12.096/174.159 = 0.06945 kg hydrogen, 197.820/174.159 = 1.13585 kg phosgene; co-products 0.83733 kg HCl and 0.62064 kg water. Mass balance: 2.45797 kg in, 2.45797 kg out. Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990. Amounts are fixed, not fitted: the stoichiometric floor at 100 % conversion. One input is an aggregated dataset - 'Toluene, liquid, at plant', itself an unflagged PlasticsEurope eco-profile whose own rebuild is blocked by the BTX allocation (see its locate response) - so the structural check flags a dependency, correctly. The sulphuric acid of the mixed-acid nitration is regenerated and is a recorded gap; so are the 0.837 kg of HCl co-product per kg of TDI, for which nothing in the bundle states an allocation. BAFU's nitric-acid dataset is declared per kg of HNO3, not of the 50 % solution - checked against 'Adipic acid, at plant', which carries 0.431 kg of it against a stoichiometric 0.862 kg, i.e. exactly half, consistent with the NOx recovery that route runs on.

replaces.name: Polyvinylchloride, suspension polymerised, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. Suspension polymerisation is carried out in an aqueous phase with a suspension stabiliser, and both the water and the stabiliser are gaps here: the dataset's own text names neither, and nothing in the bundle quantifies them. Only the monomer, the energy and the transport are modelled. Re-point the monomer to 99a93e93-...-disagg with the input's `sandbox` field to chain this onto the VCM rebuild.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymerisation process, upstream processes like ethylene, chlorine, and VCM production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.'

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: S-PVC 54.49 MJ/kg against Vinyl chloride 49.71 MJ/kg - about 4.8 MJ/kg for the suspension polymerisation step, 9 % of the total. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polyvinylchloride, suspension polymerised, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyvinylchloride, suspension polymerised, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Vinyl chloride, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: Polycarbonate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the two monomers the dataset names, amounts from the polycondensation equation with molar masses, utilities calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's own ecoSpold technology field is unusually specific - 'production by interfacial polycondesation out of phosgene and bisphenol A' - and names both reagents and the process variant, and BAFU carries a real unit process for each ('Bisphenol A, powder, at plant', 7 inputs; 'Phosgene, liquid, at plant', 7 inputs), so this model terminates on the database with no aggregated dependency at all. Amounts are the polycondensation stoichiometry: C15H16O2 (bisphenol A, 228.291) + COCl2 (phosgene, 98.910) -> -[C16H14O3]- (carbonate repeat unit, 254.285) + 2 HCl (72.916); mass balance 327.201 = 327.201. Per kg of polycarbonate: 228.291/254.285 = 0.89777 kg of bisphenol A and 98.910/254.285 = 0.38897 kg of phosgene, releasing 0.28675 kg of HCl. In the interfacial process the HCl is taken up by caustic soda, 2 NaOH per repeat unit = 2 x 39.997 / 254.285 = 0.31459 kg. Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990. The caustic soda is not named by the technology field; it is included because the field says *interfacial* polycondensation, which by definition runs the bisphenol as its disodium salt in an aqueous phase against phosgene in dichloromethane, and the HCl released must be neutralised. Two named-but-unquantified pieces are left out and recorded as gaps: the dichloromethane solvent (recycled, so its net consumption is a make-up rate nothing prints) and the chain terminator/catalyst. All three amounts are fixed, not fitted: they are the stoichiometric floor at 100 % conversion, so the true values can only be higher.

replaces.name: Ethylene glycol, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: vintage transfer: the ecoinvent v2 unit process of the same product, transcribed from its report table and verified against the two co-products BAFU still carries
strategy.note: The cited report (Rajabihamedani 2025) prints no unit process - it documents only the post-processing of a PlasticsEurope system process (see specs/evidence/582ad303-.../response-0-locate.json). The inventory here is transcribed from Althaus 2007, ecoinvent report No. 8, Tab. 35.3, which documents the multi-output process 'ethylene oxide, in ethylene glycol plant' that ecoinvent v2 used for this same dataset name, and allocated to MEG with the report's own 85 % price-times-mass factor over its 0.825 kg of MEG. The transcription is verified, not assumed: applying the same table with the DEG factor (7 %/0.1 kg) and the TEG factor (8 %/0.04 kg) reproduces BAFU's own 'Diethylene glycol, at plant' and 'Triethylene glycol, at plant' unit processes on all eleven exchanges the table covers - exactly on nine of them (ethylene oxide 0.4921 kg, electricity 0.2639 kWh, chemical plant 2.8E-10, waste heat 0.945 MJ, acetaldehyde 9.8E-07, ethylene 4.2E-06, water 0.0042 m3, and the TEG column 1.406 / 0.754 / 8E-10) and to 0.15 % on the two four-digit ones (COD/BOD 2.013E-04 against 2.016E-04, TOC/DOC 5.248E-05 against 5.250E-05). The twelfth exchange, the waterborne water emission, is not in Tab. 35.3 at all and is taken from the co-products' own 0.95 ratio. This is S2 and not S1 because the BAFU dataset being rebuilt is the PlasticsEurope 2019 eco-profile (reference year 2023), a different data generation from the 1997-2000 ecoinvent v2 inventory transcribed here; the structure is the same product's, the vintage is not. Steam is calibrated because Tab. 35.3 omits it and sec. 35.6.2 says so explicitly, and the infrastructure is calibrated between 0 and the transcribed 4.1212E-10 because the ethylene-oxide precursor already carries one chemical plant of its own.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 35.3 (printed p. 307, PDF p. 388), ch. 35 Ethylene Glycol
evidence.note: Multi-output process 'ethylene oxide, in ethylene glycol plant' [RER], per 1 kg: ethylene oxide, at plant 7.03E-1 kg; electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid 3.77E-1 kWh; chemical plant, organics 4.00E-10 unit; Water, unspecified natural origin 6.00E-03 m3; Heat, waste 1.35E+00 MJ; Acetaldehyde 1.40E-06 kg; Ethene 6.00E-06 kg; BOD5 2.88E-04 kg; COD 2.88E-01 kg (see note below); DOC 7.50E-05 kg; TOC 7.50E-05 kg. Outputs diethylene glycol 0.1 kg, ethylene glycol 0.825 kg, triethylene glycol 0.04 kg, with the allocation row 7 / 85 / 8 %. Every amount below is that column times 0.85/0.825 = 1.030303.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'It is assumed that an average 82.5% of the glycols consists of MEG. This report assumes that a further 10% is DEG, the remainder being TEG and heavy glycols.' Tab. 35.2 gives Input: Ethylene oxide 703, Output: MEG 825, DEG 100, TEG 40, Heavy glycols 35 (kg), with price x mass allocation factors 85 / 7 / 8 %. Sec. 35.5 notes the wider IPPC range: 'the glycol products typically consists of 70 - 95% w/w of MEG' - the 82.5 % split is one point in it.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'It must be assumed that some steam is utilized for glycol distillation. No figures are given. Electrical energy consumption is given as 0.377 kWh / kg in (BUWAL 232).' The steam input is therefore in the model but calibrated, unbounded - the report names it and refuses to quantify it.

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Diethylene glycol, at plant [RER] and Triethylene glycol, at plant [RER]
evidence.note: Both are 3-input unit processes still in BAFU-2026 and are the co-products of the very table transcribed here. Tab. 35.3 x 0.07/0.1 gives ethylene oxide 0.4921 kg, electricity 0.2639 kWh, chemical plant 2.80E-10 unit, water 0.0042 m3, waste heat 0.945 MJ, acetaldehyde 9.8E-07, ethylene 4.2E-06, BOD 2.016E-04, COD 2.016E-04, DOC/TOC 5.25E-05 - which is exactly what BAFU's DEG carries (0.4921 / 0.2639 / 2.8E-10 / 0.0042 / 0.945 / 9.8E-07 / 4.2E-06 / 2.013E-04 / 2.013E-04 / 5.248E-05). Same for TEG at 0.08/0.04 (EO 1.406, electricity 0.754, plant 8E-10). Two consequences: the transcription is verified, and the report's COD of 2.88E-01 kg is a typo for 2.88E-04 (the co-products carry BOD = COD), which is what is used here. The co-products also fix the water balance, 0.00399/0.0042 = 0.95 of the water input leaving as a waterborne emission; Tab. 35.3 gives only the input.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.note: 'For all datasets, the inventory regarding infrastructure contributions was checked and supplemented. For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The BAFU target indeed carries 4.0E-10 p, and Tab. 35.3 gives the same 4.00E-10 unit - the two vintages agree on this one input.

nodes.name: Ethylene glycol, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Ethylene glycol, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Unit process of the glycol section of an integrated EO/EG plant, per kg of MEG. Althaus 2007 Tab. 35.3 x 0.85/0.825. Steam calibrated (the report names it and gives no figure). The waste-treatment services and the infrastructure that BAFU's own aggregated dataset already carries explicitly are deliberately NOT copied into this model except for the infrastructure the report states; the point of the rebuild is the production chain, which is the part that was collapsed away.

technosphere.comment: Tab. 35.3 'ethylene oxide, at plant' 7.03E-01 kg x 0.85/0.825; precursor, reaction (2) C2H4O + H2O -> HO-C2H4-OH

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid
technosphere.comment: Tab. 35.3 'electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid' 3.77E-01 kWh x 0.85/0.825 (BUWAL 232); UCTE -> the ENTSO-E successor dataset BAFU carries
technosphere.supplier_name: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid

technosphere.comment: Tab. 35.3 4.00E-10 unit x 0.85/0.825 = 4.1212E-10, and Rajabihamedani sec. 3.6 gives the same 4.0E-10 p for the target - both vintages agree on it, which is why that is the upper bound. It is a bound and not the amount because 'Ethylene oxide, at plant' already carries its own 4.0E-10, and this one exchange is where 1316 of the target's 1790 cumulative flows get more than 90 % of their value from, so stacking two doubles three quarters of the vector; the fit decides how much of it belongs here (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py).

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
technosphere.comment: sec. 35.6.2: 'It must be assumed that some steam is utilized for glycol distillation. No figures are given.' Named by the report, not quantified -> calibrated, unbounded. The 0.5 start value is arbitrary and is overwritten by the fit.
technosphere.supplier_name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

biosphere.comment: Tab. 35.3 1.40E-06 kg x 0.85/0.825 (IPPC Chemicals 2002, table 9.9 point sources)
Tab. 35.3 prints 'COD' 2.88E-01 kg; BAFU's DEG/TEG co-products carry COD = BOD, so the printed exponent is a typo for 2.88E-04. x 0.85/0.825
not in Tab. 35.3; the ecoinvent v2 water balance, 0.00399/0.0042 = 0.95 of the water input, read off BAFU's DEG and TEG co-products
Tab. 35.3 'Water, unspecified natural origin' 6.00E-03 m3 x 0.85/0.825

residual.name: Ethylene glycol, at plant, disaggregated, hybrid
residual.note: Hybrid node: the explicit exchanges above plus these residual elementary flows, so that the cumulative inventory of the hybrid node equals the original BAFU system process exactly. The residual is what the explicit model does NOT yet explain.

replaces.name: Styrene-acrylonitrile copolymer, SAN, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the two monomers named by the product, split fitted under a 1 kg mass constraint, utilities calibrated
strategy.note:
NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field says 'production by different polymerization processes out of its different monomers' - it asserts that the monomers are the input list but does not name them; the product name does: styrene-acrylonitrile copolymer. Both monomers exist in BAFU, acrylonitrile as a real 9-input unit process ('Acrylonitrile from Sohio process, at plant'), styrene only as an unflagged eco-profile. Addition copolymerisation loses no mass, so the two add up to 1.000 kg, which is imposed with mass_sum; the split is nowhere quantified in the bundle and is therefore fitted, not measured - flagged low confidence. The same caveat as HIPS applies: a good inventory fit here would not prove the split is right.

AFTER THE FIT - READ THIS BEFORE USING THE AMOUNTS. The calibration was run and its result is structurally wrong, which is worth more than the spec was: the fit drove acrylonitrile to 1.2E-10 kg, i.e. zero, and put the whole kilogram on styrene - a styrene-acrylonitrile copolymer modelled as pure polystyrene. The inventory agreement it buys is poor anyway: 3 of 1668 determined flows within +-10 %, median |delta| 133 %. This is the identifiability trap the project's own calibration benchmark predicts (README sec. 6: 'a better inventory fit with the wrong structure'), caught here on real data rather than on a synthetic case. The mechanism is specific and repeatable: under a mass constraint, when one candidate monomer is another dataset of the same APME eco-profile family and another is an ecoinvent unit process, the fit will empty the ecoinvent one, because it drags in a full background of ~1670 elementary flows that the target's ~145-substance eco-profile simply does not have, and every one of them counts against the fit. And among same-family candidates the fit follows the waste-treatment exchanges, not the chemistry - which is why it prefers polybutadiene to styrene: 'Styrene, at plant' declares 0.5615 kg of hazardous waste to incineration per kg, 80x what its own polymer GPPS declares (0.0070 kg) and 250x its own feedstock benzene (0.0022 kg), so any node that links styrene inherits a waste chain the target does not have. Conclusion for a user: the node's *inventory* is a fair reconstruction of the target's flows, its *composition* is not a statement about the product, and the split must not be quoted. The amounts are left exactly as the fit produced them - no bound was moved after the score was seen.

replaces.name: Polyethylene, HDPE, granulate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. HDPE is made by low-pressure catalytic polymerisation, LDPE by the high-pressure radical route and LLDPE by low-pressure copolymerisation with an alpha-olefin. The bundle documents none of that quantitatively, so the three specs differ only in what the fit puts into electricity and steam. The alpha-olefin comonomer of LLDPE (a few per cent of 1-butene/1-hexene) is a known gap: no dataset for it is named anywhere and folding it into the ethylene is the standard simplification.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like ethylene production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' - the whole input list the dataset declares.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: HDPE 77.38 MJ/kg against Ethylene, average 70.73 MJ/kg, so the whole gate-to-gate step the fit has to find is worth about 6.7 MJ/kg, under 9 % of the total. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polyethylene, HDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyethylene, HDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Ethylene, average, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: xx Acetone cyanohydrin, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the two reagents the dataset names, amounts from the addition equation with molar masses, utilities calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. Althaus (2007) lists this dataset in Tab. 1.1 as 'Reported in: Part II', but the 957-page report has no acetone-cyanohydrin chapter - the index points at a chapter the report does not contain (see the locate response). The dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, 'production from acetone and hydrogen cyanide by base-catalyzed reaction', names both reagents and the catalysis. C3H6O (acetone, 58.080) + HCN (27.026) -> C4H7NO (acetone cyanohydrin, 85.106); a pure addition, 85.106 = 85.106, so the two reagents add up to exactly 1.000 kg per kg of product: 58.080/85.106 = 0.68244 kg of acetone and 27.026/85.106 = 0.31756 kg of hydrogen cyanide. Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990. This is the one reaction in the whole set with no co-product and no yield ambiguity: it is a 1:1 addition and the masses close exactly, so the amounts are fixed. Both reagents are themselves unflagged eco-profiles in this same set - and both are rebuilt here from the Althaus report (acetone from the cumene figure, hydrogen cyanide from Tab. 43.2/43.3/43.4) - so this is the deepest chain in the set. It is linked to the BAFU datasets rather than to those rebuilds so that its check measures its own evidence; re-point with `sandbox` to chain them. The base catalyst is a gap: named, never quantified.

replaces.name: Styrene, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: ethylbenzene by the dehydrogenation equation with molar masses, utilities from the BAFU chemicals template and calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The input list comes from the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, 'mixture of process of dehydrogenation of ethyl benzene and oxirane process', and the amount from the dehydrogenation equation C6H5C2H5 -> C6H5CH=CH2 + H2: 106.168/104.152 = 1.01936 kg of ethylbenzene per kg of styrene at full conversion, with 0.01936 kg of hydrogen released. That is the stoichiometric floor - industrial reactors run 60-70 % conversion per pass with recycle, so the gross feed is higher but the net consumption per kg of product is this - and it is fixed, not fitted. The second route the field names, the oxirane (propylene-oxide/styrene-monomer) process, is not modelled: it is a two-product process whose share and allocation neither the field nor any bundled report gives, and folding it in would require inventing both. Said plainly: this model is the dehydrogenation route only. Dehydrogenation is strongly endothermic - about 1.2 MJ per kg of styrene of reaction enthalpy alone, before the steam dilution the process runs on - so the template's 2.0 MJ is certainly too low, which is precisely why heat and electricity are left free. The reason to do this one first: styrene is the monomer of GPPS, HIPS, SAN, ABS and the already-committed expandable-polystyrene spec, and 'Ethyl benzene, at plant' is a real 7-input BAFU unit process, so the chain terminates on the database. One level further down, ethylbenzene's own benzene input is itself an unflagged eco-profile whose rebuild is blocked by the BTX allocation - that is a finding about the database, not something this spec can fix.

The cited report is only the 17-page front matter of ecoinvent report No. 11; all 114 bundled reports were converted with pdftotext and searched.

replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the balanced VCM process, input list from the dataset's own process description, amounts from the reaction stoichiometry, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory (see the evidence block). The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself states - 'The VCM production process, upstream processes like ethylene and chlorine production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment' - and the two material amounts follow from the balanced-process equations printed in Althaus 2007 sec. 34.5.3 with the yields of sec. 34.5.1. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere in the bundle, so they are fitted, unbounded. No direct process emissions are modelled: the only VCM emission factors in the bundle (Althaus Tab. 34.1) are for EDC, not for the cracking step.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The VCM production process, upstream processes like ethylene and chlorine production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' - this is the whole input list the dataset declares, and it is what the model contains.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H4Cl2 (Chlorination of ethylene to EDC) / C2H4Cl -> CH2CHCl + HCl (Cracking of EDC to form VCM) / C2H4 + 1/2 O2 + 2HCl -> C2H4Cl2 + H2O (Oxychlorination route to EDC)'. 'Often all the HCl generated in the cracking section is reused in producing EDC by oxychlorination. Plants that exhibit this characteristic and also do not export EDC are called “balanced”. The balanced process is the common process used as a Best Available Technology benchmark.' Summing the three gives the balanced overall reaction 2 C2H4 + Cl2 + 1/2 O2 -> 2 C2H3Cl + H2O, in which the HCl cancels - which is why VCM is modelled here from ethylene and chlorine directly and not from 1.583 kg of EDC (that route would double-count the chlorine, because half of it comes back as HCl).

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.where: sec. 34.5.1 EDC by direct chlorination of ethylene
evidence.note: 'Yield on ethylene 96-98% / on chlorine 98%' - the midpoint 97 % and the 98 % are applied to the stoichiometric amounts.

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Ethylene dichloride, at plant [RER]
evidence.note: The one BAFU unit process for the same chemistry carries 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg, chlorine, liquid, production mix 0.735 kg and ethylene 0.295 kg - it reproduces Althaus Tab. 34.3 exactly, which is the check that this way of reading the report gives back the dataset it built.

nodes.name: Vinyl chloride, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Vinyl chloride, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Balanced EDC/VCM process, per kg of vinyl chloride monomer. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Ethylene, average, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1.042 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: Nylon 66, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model, deliberately incomplete: adipic acid by the polycondensation equation; the diamine has no dataset in BAFU-2026
strategy.note: NOT S1, and not complete either - read this before using the node. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field names both monomers - 'production out of hexamethylene diamine and adipic acid' - and the polycondensation equation gives both amounts exactly: Polycondensation: C6H10O4 (adipic acid, 146.142) + C6H16N2 (hexamethylenediamine, 116.208) -> -[C12H22N2O2]- (nylon-6,6 repeat unit, 226.320) + 2 H2O (36.030); 262.350 = 262.350. Per kg of nylon 6,6: 146.142/226.320 = 0.64573 kg of adipic acid and 116.208/226.320 = 0.51347 kg of hexamethylenediamine, releasing 0.15921 kg of water. Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990. Only one of the two can be linked: 'Adipic acid, at plant' [RER] is a real 7-input BAFU unit process, but BAFU-2026 contains no hexamethylenediamine dataset at all, and no adiponitrile or hexanedinitrile either - searched by name over all 11,947 datasets. So this model carries 0.646 kg of the 1.159 kg of monomer the reaction needs, i.e. 56 % of the input mass and none of the nitrogen; the missing 0.513 kg of diamine is not a rounding gap but half the chemistry, and it is why the flow agreement of this node must not be read as a quality statement about the method. It is published rather than withheld because the adipic-acid half is exact and because the missing half is named, quantified and traceable: anyone who adds a hexamethylenediamine dataset can complete it by adding one line.

The cited report is only the 17-page front matter of ecoinvent report No. 11; all 114 bundled reports were converted with pdftotext and searched.

replaces.name: Naphtha, APME mix, at refinery
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: template transfer: BAFU's own refinery unit process for the same product, at the same location
strategy.note:
S2, not S1: no report in the bundle prints an inventory for the APME mix (the locate response records the search). What makes this one reachable anyway is that BAFU-2026 already contains a unit process of the same product at the same location - 'Naphtha, at refinery' [RER], 33 technosphere inputs and 126 elementary flows, the ecoinvent refinery model documented in 2007 - Crude oil - Jungbluth.pdf. The two datasets differ in provenance, not in product: the target is PlasticsEurope's own cumulated refinery figure for the naphtha its members buy ('product out of refining process of oil and gas', ecoSpold technology field), the sibling is ecoinvent's model of the same European refinery slate. Substituting one for the other is exactly the template transfer S2 describes, and it is a 1:1 substitution because both are 1 kg of naphtha at the refinery gate - there is no region, scale or vintage to adapt, so nothing is calibrated and there is no free amount in this spec at all. What the check then measures is a real question about the database: how far apart are PlasticsEurope's and ecoinvent's naphtha? Caveat: the target is the APME *mix*, which may be sourced differently from the ecoinvent RER slate, and nothing in the bundle says how.

AFTER THE CHECK. The question this spec was written to answer - how far apart are PlasticsEurope's and ecoinvent's naphtha? - has an answer, and it is: far. Fossil CO2 agrees to -16 %, but every other headline flow of the APME profile is far higher than the ecoinvent refinery model produces: methane -98.9 %, NMVOC -98.3 %, nitrogen oxides -84.8 %, carbon monoxide -82.3 %, sulfur dioxide -74.7 %. In other words the APME naphtha carries roughly 50-100x the methane and NMVOC of ecoinvent's, at comparable CO2. Overall: 0 of the 50 largest kilogram flows within +-10 %, 4 of 1668 determined flows. The two datasets are not interchangeable, and this spec's value is that it says so with numbers rather than leaving the substitution to be made silently downstream.
