replaces.name: Xylene, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: BREF ranges for a reformate xylene plant, feedstock split from the dataset's own text, every free amount bounded by a printed range
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. Althaus 2007 ch. 96 is about this very dataset name, but its inventory tables 96.5-96.7 are the *cumulative* vector of the PlasticsEurope module - the report says so: 'Due to the fact that this dataset is cumulated it was not possible to use the other processes modelled in ecoinvent to obtain a transparent process chain' - so they are the aggregate this project is trying to open, not a unit process. What ch. 96 does print, from the EU BREF (European Commission 2002), is a gate-to-gate picture of a reformate xylene plant as ranges: Tab. 96.1 consumptions and yields, Tab. 96.2 air emissions, Tab. 96.3 wastewater, Tab. 96.4 solid wastes. That is what is modelled here. Every free amount carries bounds taken straight from those printed ranges - none of them was chosen to make the agreement look better, and the feedstock bounds in particular are very wide (1.37-4.35 kg per kg) because the printed yield range is. Same caveat as Althaus's own: 'Within the module assessed here there are only the resources and emissions considered which are given in the data source. Therefore no land use could be included and no direct soil emissions within the process chain are stated.'

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (technology)
evidence.note: 'Xylenes are commercially produced based on two different feedstocks: - Pyrolysis gasoline, a side product of thermal cracking (steam cracking) of hydrocarbons (e.g. naphtha, gas oil, ethane, propane, butanes, natural gas liquids) - Reformate, a product of catalytic reforming of naphtha. ... In Europe (EU27) xylenes are mainly produced via pyrolysis gasoline (14 %) and reformate (86 %).' The 14/86 split is the only quantitative statement about this dataset anywhere, and it fixes the feedstock mix.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: 'Energy usage for and precursor materials for xylene production (European Commission (2002))', column 'Reformate plant', per ton of feedstock: Fuel gas 3 - 10 kg; Steam (tons) 0.5 - 1.5; Electricity (MWh) <0.07. Production (tons) per ton of feedstock: p-xylene 0.23 - 0.48; o-xylene 0 - 0.25. Summing the two product ranges gives 0.23 - 0.73 t of xylenes per t of feedstock, i.e. 1.370 - 4.348 kg of feedstock per kg of product, and every consumption range is multiplied by that to get a per-kg-of-product range.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 96.2 and Tab. 96.3 (same page), row 'BTX from aromatic mixture (source: a single plant)'
evidence.note: Air, kg/ton product: Methane 0.086; SO2 0.53; Particulates 0.008 kg/ton *feedstock*; VOC 0.03 toluene and 0.2 NMVOCtot. Water, kg/ton product: Benzene 0.003; Toluene 0.001; COD 0.087; N-Kjeldahl 0.0009. Two rows are not used: the particulates, because they are per ton of feedstock and the feedstock amount here is itself calibrated, and the second 'Methane' column (0.09), because the table has two columns with that same header and the report gives no way to tell what the second one is. The caption reads 'Air emissions for toluene production' inside the xylenes chapter, which is a copy-paste slip in the report; the rows are the BTX plant the chapter is about.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: kg/ton product: Catalysts 0.05 'recycled via supplier'; Clay, desiccant material, inert balls 0.006 'reused after regeneration'; Activated carbon 0.01 'incinerated'; Filter cloth etc. 0.0009 'incinerated'. The first two leave the system as recovered material and are skipped; the two incinerated streams are modelled together, since 'The wastes are usually recycled, landfilled or incinerated in a hazardous waste incinerator.'

nodes.name: Xylene, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Xylene, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Separation of mixed xylenes from reformate (86 %) and pyrolysis gasoline (14 %), per kg. Gaps: no reformate dataset exists in BAFU, so naphtha - the feed of the catalytic reformer - stands in for it and the reforming step itself is missing from the chain; particulate emissions are per ton of feedstock and cannot be fixed while the feedstock is calibrated; the isomer separation described in sec. 96.5.1 is not quantified anywhere. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Pyrolysis gasoline, production mix, at plant [RER], itself one of the 101 and the one dataset of this family that could not be rebuilt at all, which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: reformate route, 86% of EU27 xylene (dataset text) x the feedstock range of Tab. 96.1 (1.370-4.348 kg feedstock per kg product) = 1.1781-3.7391 kg; naphtha stands in for reformate, which BAFU does not have

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Pyrolysis gasoline, production mix, at plant
technosphere.comment: pygas route, 14% of EU27 xylene (dataset text) x the same feedstock range = 0.1918-0.6087 kg
technosphere.supplier_name: Pyrolysis gasoline, production mix, at plant

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
technosphere.comment: Tab. 96.1 'Steam (tons) 0.5 - 1.5' per ton of feedstock x the feedstock range = 0.6849-6.5217 kg per kg of product
technosphere.supplier_name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid
technosphere.comment: Tab. 96.1 'Electricity (MWh) <0.07' per ton of feedstock = <0.07 kWh/kg feedstock x the feedstock range = 0-0.3043 kWh per kg of product
technosphere.supplier_name: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid

technosphere.comment: Tab. 96.1 'Fuel gas 3 - 10 kg' per ton of feedstock = 0.0041-0.0435 kg per kg of product. No heating value for refinery fuel gas is printed in any report of the bundle, so the mass range cannot be converted to the megajoules this dataset is measured in; rather than invent a heating value the amount is calibrated, unbounded, and the printed mass range is recorded here instead

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Disposal, hazardous waste, 25% water, to hazardous waste incineration
technosphere.comment: Tab. 96.4: activated carbon 0.01 kg/ton product + filter cloth etc. 0.0009 kg/ton product, both marked 'incinerated' = 1.09E-05 kg/kg; catalysts (0.05, recycled via supplier) and clay/desiccant (0.006, reused after regeneration) are not disposal and are skipped
technosphere.supplier_name: Disposal, hazardous waste, 25% water, to hazardous waste incineration

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

datasets.bafu_name: Polystyrene, high impact, HIPS, at plant

replaces.name: Polystyrene, high impact, HIPS, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the two monomers named by the product, split fitted under a 1 kg mass constraint, utilities calibrated
strategy.note:
NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory for this dataset. The dataset's own ecoSpold technology field is 'polymerization out of ethylene and benzene by free radical processes' - word for word the same text as the general-purpose grade, so the field does not distinguish HIPS from GPPS at all and gives no rubber. What does distinguish them is the product name: high-impact polystyrene is polystyrene toughened with polybutadiene rubber, which is why BAFU carries a separate dataset for it and why PlasticsEurope's own 2012 eco-profile for it is titled 'High impact polystyrene (HIPS); polymerisation of polybutadiene' (quoted in Tab. 6.1 of 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf, which lists it as 'Recommended to be added' and prints no inventory). So the structure - styrene plus polybutadiene - is evidence-backed; the split is not. No number for the rubber content exists in the bundle, so both monomers are free and constrained only by mass_sum = 1.0 kg: addition polymerisation loses no mass, so whatever is not styrene is rubber. The split is therefore a fit, not a measurement, and is flagged low confidence. This is the same device the committed cement ZN spec uses for a composition given only as ranges.

AFTER THE FIT - READ THIS BEFORE USING THE AMOUNTS. The calibration was run and its result is structurally wrong, which is worth more than the spec was: the fit put 0.9998 kg on polybutadiene and 1.0E-4 kg on styrene - high-impact *polystyrene* modelled as pure rubber, where the real rubber content is a few per cent. The inventory agreement it buys is 621 of 1668 determined flows within +-10 % (37 %), median |delta| 11.3 %. This is the identifiability trap the project's own calibration benchmark predicts (README sec. 6: 'a better inventory fit with the wrong structure'), caught here on real data rather than on a synthetic case. The mechanism is specific and repeatable: under a mass constraint, when one candidate monomer is another dataset of the same APME eco-profile family and another is an ecoinvent unit process, the fit will empty the ecoinvent one, because it drags in a full background of ~1670 elementary flows that the target's ~145-substance eco-profile simply does not have, and every one of them counts against the fit. And among same-family candidates the fit follows the waste-treatment exchanges, not the chemistry - which is why it prefers polybutadiene to styrene: 'Styrene, at plant' declares 0.5615 kg of hazardous waste to incineration per kg, 80x what its own polymer GPPS declares (0.0070 kg) and 250x its own feedstock benzene (0.0022 kg), so any node that links styrene inherits a waste chain the target does not have. Conclusion for a user: the node's *inventory* is a fair reconstruction of the target's flows, its *composition* is not a statement about the product, and the split must not be quoted. The amounts are left exactly as the fit produced them - no bound was moved after the score was seen.

datasets.bafu_name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant

replaces.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft); the report's tables are published comparison data, not this dataset's inventory
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of TiO2; Tab. 85.3 is headed 'Kg per kg of product', Tab. 85.5 'Consumption per kg of product (MJ/kg)', Tab. 85.7 and Tab. 85.9 'Gram per kg of product'. The CHLORIDE-process column is used.; allocation: none stated for the TiO2 process itself; 6 of 7 inputs carry a printed amount, 1 a printed range, 0 no number in the report. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 e1b3f9c29c3269b8…

gaps_reported_by_model: Section 85.6 says 'This inventory is based on confidential information provided by industry sources. The input information may not be divulged.' The printed BAT-Notes figures are what the report compares against, not necessarily the exact dataset amounts.
No transport, no infrastructure (chemical plant) and no water input are quantified anywhere in the excerpt for the TiO2 process; they are therefore not included.
Tab. 85.5 gives no coal for the chloride process and no breakdown of which fuel produces the steam beyond the sentence about a natural gas boiler.
The excerpt gives no process water, no NOx and no organic emissions for the chloride route.
skipped_items: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant: product — Reference product; the whole excerpt is per kg of product.

nodes.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 845-847

technosphere.comment: Chloride-process precursor. The text adds 'The chloride process titanium dioxide is also assumed to stem from ilmenite, although in fact rutile, synthetic rutile and /or beneficiate are used. The data for mining of ilmenite are taken from (BUWAL 232).' so the supplying dataset is the ilmenite/rutile ore, not TiO2 itself.

provenance.quote: Synthetic rutile   ng   1.06   (Chemlink.com)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column, 'Kg per kg of product']
provenance.mapping_reason: Tab. 85.3 names 'Synthetic rutile' for the chloride route; the rutile concentrate is that material, while ilmenite is the lower-grade ore the sulfate route uses.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant
technosphere.comment: Printed value for the chloride process.
technosphere.supplier_name: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant

provenance.quote: Chlorine   na   0.18   (UBA BAT Notes, 2001)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column]
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and a production mix, as the report gives no specific electrolysis route; chlorine dioxide is a different chemical.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
technosphere.comment: 1.51 MJ (TiO2 manufacture) + 0.83 MJ (follow-up treatment) = 2.34 MJ/kg, the two columns of the same row. The text says the model facility 'imports UCTE grid electricity'.
technosphere.supplier_name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid

provenance.quote: Electric energy   1.51   0.83   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process), TiO2 manufacture + Follow-up treatment]
provenance.factor_source: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, so MJ x 0.2778 = kWh (ecoinvent convention)
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says the model plant 'imports UCTE grid electricity'; this is the UCTE production mix, beating the single-fuel UCTE variants and the RER/CH grids.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: 1.7 + 7.7 = 9.4 MJ/kg. The text: 'The model facility portrayed here uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam', so the steam is entered as natural-gas heat in MJ.
technosphere.supplier_name: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Steam   1.7   7.7   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: The report: 'uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam'; this is delivered heat in MJ from a natural-gas furnace, which matches the MJ/kg the table gives, beating the 'burned in' variants that model the combustion itself.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: 2.9 + 4.2 = 7.1 MJ/kg of direct process gas, separate from the gas burned for steam.
technosphere.supplier_name: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Gas   2.9   4.2   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: Direct process gas burned on site, which is what the separate 'Gas' row of Tab. 85.5 is, as opposed to the gas that makes the steam.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
technosphere.comment: 0.11 + 2.25 = 2.36 g/kg. Treated here as a disposal service (an input), since the report lists it under wastewater emissions but it is a solid residue. Low confidence on which disposal dataset applies.
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill

provenance.quote: Filter residues   0.11   2.25   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The disposal dataset made for exactly this residue stream of the chloride route, beating the SO4 variant and the generic residue landfills.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
technosphere.comment: The excerpt gives 184 g/kg from the BAT notes and says industry suggests up to 1 kg/kg; entered as a bounded free input over exactly that printed range.
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill

provenance.quote: Chloride process. According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001), chloride process sludges total 184 g / kg product. Industry sources however suggest somewhat higher values, ranging up to 1 kg / kg product
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Same stream as the filter residues and the only chloride-route TiO2 disposal dataset in the database.

biosphere.comment: 0.005 g (storage) + 0.186 g (follow-up treatment) = 0.191 g/kg. The report does not state a size fraction for the chloride route.

provenance.quote: Particles   0.005   ng   ng   0.186   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The only candidate; the report states no particle size fraction for TiO2, so the unspecified particulate flow is the honest choice.

biosphere.comment: The asterisk in the table marks 0.024 g/kg as the value the report actually uses for the model chloride plant.

provenance.quote: HCl   ng   0.007   0.024 *   ng   * This value is used for the model chloride plant.   [Tab. 85.7]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance in the stated air compartment; the soil and water copies are the wrong compartment and 'Chloride' is the ion, not HCl.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: SO2   ng   ng   1.68   ng   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process), off-gas treatment]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; 'Sulfur Oxides' is the aggregate and 'Sulfur' the element.

biosphere.comment: The table prints 0.011 g/kg but the footnote below it states 'This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2'; the footnote value is the one the dataset was built with.

provenance.quote: Iron   0.011 *   ng   ...   This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says only 'Iron' with no oxidation state, so the unspecified iron flow beats Iron(2+) and Iron(3+).

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Cadmium   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Cadmium(2+) presumes an oxidation state the report does not give and Cadmium-109 is a radionuclide.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Mercury   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Mercury(2+) presumes a speciation the report does not give.

strategy.label: top-down model drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of wood preservative; the table's product row reads 'wood preservative, inorganic salt, containing Cr, at plant  1.00E+00 kg'; allocation: none stated; single-product process; 3 of 8 inputs carry a printed amount, 4 a printed range, 1 no number in the report (xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid). Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI wood as fuel and const. mat. - Werner.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 1f2e06f8a69ca03e…, text sha256 207d840fb9d1bcd4…

gaps_reported_by_model: The five material amounts (boric acid, chromium oxide, copper oxide, UCTE electricity, tap water) are printed as 'confidential'. The excerpt gives no numbers for them at all; they are entered as free parameters with wide bounds and are determined by the calibration step, not by the report.
The report gives no process emissions for this dataset ('No process emission data are available' in the BAFU metadata); only the calculated waste heat is listed.

The bounds attached to the confidential rows are not from the report. They are deliberately wide search ranges (0.001-1 kg for the salts, since the product is 1 kg of mixed salts; 1e-4 to 5 kWh; 0.001-100 kg of water).

replaces.name: Purified terephthalic acid, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: p-xylene by the oxidation stoichiometry from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory and says of PTA only that a x1000 correction was applied to one land-occupation flow (sec. 3.8). The dataset's own includedProcesses field names the chemistry - 'Crude terephthalic acid (CTA) is produced by oxidation of p-xylene. A subsequent purification step leads to purified terephthalic acid (PTA)' - and the feedstock amount follows from that reaction. Two honest weaknesses: (1) the amount is the theoretical minimum, because no yield is printed anywhere in the bundle, so the model is low on p-xylene by whatever the real loss is; (2) BAFU has only 'Xylene, at plant', the mixed-isomer dataset, not p-xylene, so the isomer separation - which Althaus 2007 sec. 96.5.1 describes as crystallisation or molecular-sieve adsorption and does not quantify - is missing from the chain. The acetic acid solvent and the cobalt/manganese/bromide catalyst of the oxidation step are named by neither the dataset nor any report in the bundle and are left out rather than guessed.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses)
evidence.note: 'Crude terephthalic acid (CTA) is produced by oxidation of p-xylene. A subsequent purification step leads to purified terephthalic acid (PTA). In addition to these foreground processes, the following processes in the supply chain are considered for this EPD: extraction and refinery of crude oil and natural gas, steam cracking of hydrocarbons (predominantly naphtha) into lower olefins and pygas, catalytic reforming of naphtha, and the extraction and production of p-xylene from both pygas and reformate (xylene loop).'

evidence.source: stoichiometry of the p-xylene oxidation
evidence.note: C8H10 + 3 O2 -> C8H6O4 + 2 H2O. Per kg of PTA: M(C8H10)/M(C8H6O4) = 106.165/166.131 = 0.6390 kg of p-xylene. The oxygen is taken from air and is not an inventoried input, as in every air-oxidation process in BAFU (cf. Ethylene oxide, at plant, whose oxygen is a purchased pure-O2 input and is therefore listed there but not here).

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: Describes the isomer separation that this model cannot represent: 'Crystallization techniques take advantage of the spread of melting points ... p-Xylene can also be recovered using solid absorption of the molecular-sieve type.' No amounts are given for it anywhere.

nodes.name: Purified terephthalic acid, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Purified terephthalic acid, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Air oxidation of p-xylene to CTA plus purification to PTA, per kg. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Xylene, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: C8H10 + 3 O2 -> C8H6O4 + 2 H2O: 106.165/166.131 = 0.6390 kg, the theoretical minimum (no yield printed in the bundle); mixed xylene stands in for p-xylene, see the strategy note

technosphere.supplier_name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 0.639 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

replaces.name: Methylene diphenyl diisocyanate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the three reagents the dataset names, amounts from the two reaction equations with molar masses, utilities calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field names the complete reagent list - 'production out of phosgene, aniline and formaldehyde' - and BAFU carries a real unit process for each one ('Phosgene, liquid, at plant', 'Aniline, at plant', 'Formaldehyde, production mix, at plant'), so this model terminates on the database with no aggregated dependency. Two steps, both named by the technology field. Condensation: 2 C6H7N (aniline, 186.258) + CH2O (formaldehyde, 30.026) -> C13H14N2 (methylenedianiline, 198.269) + H2O (18.015); 216.284 = 216.284. Phosgenation: C13H14N2 + 2 COCl2 (197.820) -> C15H10N2O2 (MDI, 250.257) + 4 HCl (145.832); 396.089 = 396.089. Per kg of MDI: 186.258/250.257 = 0.74426 kg aniline, 30.026/250.257 = 0.11998 kg formaldehyde, 197.820/250.257 = 0.79046 kg phosgene; co-products 0.58273 kg HCl and 0.07199 kg water. Mass balance of the whole model: 1.6547 kg in, 1.6547 kg out. Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990. The hydrogen chloride co-product (0.583 kg per kg of MDI, more than half the product mass) is recorded in this note and given no credit, because nothing in the bundle states an allocation. Amounts are fixed, not fitted: they are the stoichiometric floor at 100 % conversion. Known gaps: the hydrochloric acid catalyst of the condensation step and the chlorobenzene/monochlorobenzene solvent of the phosgenation, both recycled and neither quantified anywhere; and the polymeric-MDI fraction, which the dataset does not distinguish.

replaces.name: Polyethylene, LDPE, granulate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like ethylene production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' - the whole input list the dataset declares.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: LDPE 79.41 MJ/kg against Ethylene, average 70.73 MJ/kg - about 8.7 MJ/kg for the high-pressure polymerisation step, 11 % of the total. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polyethylene, LDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyethylene, LDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Ethylene, average, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

datasets.bafu_name: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant

replaces.name: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: template transfer from BAFU's own PET-granulate-amorphous unit process, the six energy inputs calibrated within 0.5-2x
strategy.note: The cited report prints no inventory. BAFU-2026 does carry a 16-input unit process for the same polymer in its other grade - 'Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, amorphous, at plant' [RER] - and the target declares exactly that structure: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like pX, PTA, and MEG production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' Bottle grade differs from amorphous by a solid-state polycondensation step, which is extra heat and residence time and no extra material; the six energy inputs are therefore free within 0.5-2x of the template (the bound convention of the committed gypsum-fibre-board S2 spec) and the three material inputs are fixed. This is the best-evidenced of the family after ethylene glycol, and it is the only one of the fourteen whose direct process emissions are known at all - they come with the template.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like pX, PTA, and MEG production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.'

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, amorphous, at plant [RER] (unit process, 16 inputs, 15 direct flows)
evidence.note: Per kg: purified terephthalic acid 0.875 kg, ethylene glycol 0.334 kg, nitrogen liquid 0.0298 kg, steam 0.94 kg, electricity 0.194 kWh, heat natural gas 0.665 MJ, heat heavy fuel oil 0.494 MJ, heat hard coal 0.306 MJ, heat light fuel oil 0.165 MJ, chemical plant organics 4.0E-10 unit, transport rail 0.743 tkm + lorry 0.124 tkm, four disposal services, and 15 direct elementary flows. The four disposal services are dropped here: the bottle-grade target declares no waste-treatment exchanges at all (its only technosphere exchange is the 4.0E-10 chemical plant), so copying them in would add a chain the dataset does not have.

evidence.source: stoichiometry of the PET esterification
evidence.where: cross-check of the two material amounts
evidence.note: n HOOC-C6H4-COOH + n HO-C2H4-OH -> [-OC-C6H4-CO-O-C2H4-O-]n + 2n H2O. Per kg of repeat unit (M = 192.17): PTA 166.131/192.17 = 0.8645 kg, MEG 62.068/192.17 = 0.3230 kg. The template sits 1.2 % and 3.4 % above those minima, which is the expected order for process losses - the template is consistent with the chemistry, which is why both are kept fixed rather than fitted.

nodes.name: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyethylene terephthalate, granulate, bottle grade, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Esterification/polycondensation of PTA and MEG plus the solid-state step, per kg of bottle-grade granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Purified terephthalic acid, at plant [RER] and Ethylene glycol, at plant [RER], both of them among the 101, which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of liquid epoxy resin, the column header of Tab. 31.2; allocation: None stated; Tab. 31.2 has a single output, 'epoxy resin, liquid, disaggregated data, at plant, 1.00E+0 kg'.; 9 of 9 inputs carry a printed amount, 0 a printed range, 0 no number in the report. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 bb4176808c838003…

gaps_reported_by_model: Tab. 31.2 is a partial disaggregation, not a full unit process: Boustead's cumulative energy and waste have been pulled out into technosphere exchanges (electricity, heavy fuel oil, natural gas furnace, tap water, two disposal services, transport, chemical plant), but the chemistry has not - there is no epichlorohydrin and no bisphenol A line, although the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field says 'Production from epichlorohydrin and bisphenol-A' and BAFU carries unit processes for both ('Epichlorohydrin, from hypochlorination of allyl chloride, at plant' and 'Bisphenol A, powder, at plant'). What is left in the elementary flows below - 1.8 kg of rock salt, 0.98 kg of chloride to water, 0.38 kg of sodium to water - is the chlor-alkali chain of the epichlorohydrin still sitting in the direct flows.
1200 kg of sand per kg of resin (see the item note) is transcribed as printed and is almost certainly wrong in the source.

Six of the eight waste-treatment services that the aggregated dataset carries (spoil from coal mining, incineration residue, hazardous waste to underground deposit, facilities chemical production, plastics to sanitary landfill, wood to incineration, tailings) appear in Tab. 31.1 but not in Tab. 31.2, which keeps only the two municipal-solid-waste lines.
No land use and no soil emissions, as chapter 31 says for the whole Boustead family.
The report gives no uncertainty ('Uncertainty for LCI results cannot be determined' on every line).
skipped_items: Water, unspecified natural origin: no flow chosen (The deterministic keyword search returned no candidate at all for this phrase (every word of it is a stop-word-like token in the flow index), so there is nothing to choose from. The intended flow is EF 3.1 'Water' in 'Renewable material resources from water' - it is visible in the candidate list of the sibling item 'Water, river' - but the rules forbid picking a candidate that was not offered for this item, so it is recorded as missing. 6.10E-3 m3 per kg is lost.)

Hydrogen fluoride: no flow chosen (none of the offered candidates is hydrogen fluoride in an air compartment: the list holds hydrogen fluoride only to soil and to water (long-term), plus hydrogen, tritium and fluoride ion. Rather than release 5E-7 kg of HF into the wrong compartment or map it to a different substance, it is left unmapped.)

Methane, chlorotrifluoro-, CFC-13: no flow chosen (the deterministic search returned no candidate at all for this name, so there is nothing to choose; 8E-6 kg of CFC-13 per kg of resin is lost, which matters more than its mass suggests because it is a very high-GWP halocarbon.)

strategy.note:
The one case in the whole set where the answer is already inside the database. Chapter 31 of 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf prints two inventories of liquid epoxy resin side by side: Tab. 31.1, 'Life cycle inventory ... based on cumulative data', which is the target, and Tab. 31.2, 'Disaggregated life cycle inventory for the production of liquid epoxy resin (modified from Boustead 1999)', which is the same product as a unit process - 9 technosphere exchanges plus its own resources and direct emissions. BAFU-2026 carries both: the target, and 'Epoxy resin, liquid, disaggregated data, at plant' [RER] (code 6ac7f2be, 9 inputs, 63 elementary flows), whose exchanges reproduce Tab. 31.2 line for line - checked one by one: 2.19 kWh electricity, 11.0 MJ heavy fuel oil, 57.7 MJ natural-gas furnace, 13.0 kg tap water, 0.298 and 0.0058 kg of the two disposal services, 4.0E-10 chemical plant, 1.74 tkm rail, 60.6 tkm lorry. So this spec links that node 1:1 and calibrates nothing. A parallel spec, specs/c80b8e9e-epoxy-resin-liquid-at-plant.draft.json, transcribes Tab. 31.2 through the LLM route instead; the two should agree, and where they do not the difference is transcription or flow mapping, which is worth knowing. What the check measures here is not how good this project's method is - it is how far BAFU's own disaggregated dataset lands from BAFU's own aggregated one for the same product, which is the cleanest available answer to 'what does disaggregation cost?'. One thing to expect: the two BAFU datasets put their air emissions in different sub-compartments - the aggregated one in 'Emissions to urban air close to ground', the disaggregated one in 'Emissions to air, unspecified' - so a substance total that is exactly right can still score as two large deviations.

AFTER THE CHECK. The result is the most useful number this batch produced, because it is a control with no modelling in it at all: BAFU's own disaggregated epoxy resin against BAFU's own aggregated epoxy resin, 1 kg for 1 kg. On the substances that carry the dataset it is close - fossil CO2 +1.5 %, rock salt +3.6 %, chloride to water +11.2 %, sodium to water +11.8 %, suspended solids -13.7 %, calcium +18.4 %, calcite +53.2 % - and it covers 75 % of the target's kilogram mass. On the project's headline metric it scores 6 of 1669 determined flows within +-10 %, i.e. 0 %. Both numbers are correct and they measure different things: the second is dominated by ~1500 trace flows that exist only because the two datasets reach different backgrounds, and by the sub-compartment split between them (the aggregated dataset puts its air emissions in 'Emissions to urban air close to ground', the disaggregated one in 'Emissions to air, unspecified', so a substance total that is exactly right scores as two large deviations). Anyone reading a low 'share of flows within 10 %' for this family should compare it with this row first.

replaces.name: Benzene, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: template transfer: BAFU's own refinery unit process for the same product, at another location
strategy.note:
S2, not S1 and not S3. The locate response records why no report route exists: Althaus Tab. 1.1 lists 'benzene, at plant RER' as 'Reported in: Part II' and the 957-page report has no benzene chapter, and what it does print about benzene - chapter 86, Tab. 86.1, 'Production (tons) per ton of feedstock: Benzene 0.12 - 0.24, Toluene 0 - 0.3' - is a multi-product BTX plant with no allocation stated. Stoichiometry does not help either: catalytic reforming is not one reaction. What does exist is a unit process of the same product elsewhere in BAFU-2026: 'Benzene, at refinery' [CH], code d0a00133, 32 technosphere inputs and 74 elementary flows - ecoinvent's refinery model, documented in 2007 - Crude oil - Jungbluth.pdf, in which benzene is a co-product of the refinery slate whose allocation ecoinvent resolved its own way. Transferring it 1:1 does not solve the allocation problem of the APME benzene; it replaces it with ecoinvent's, which at least is documented. Two caveats a user must carry: the template is CH, not RER (there is no RER variant, and a Swiss refinery is not a European average), and the two datasets are different vintages of a different industry survey. Nothing is calibrated - there is no free amount in this spec at all - so the check measures exactly one thing: how far apart PlasticsEurope's benzene and ecoinvent's benzene are. That matters beyond this row, because benzene is the feedstock of BAFU's 'Ethyl benzene, at plant' and 'Cumene, at plant', i.e. of the styrene and acetone chains rebuilt in the same batch, and they terminate on it.

AFTER THE CHECK - and this is the number the spec was written to get. PlasticsEurope's benzene and ecoinvent's refinery benzene are not close: per kg of benzene the target carries 1.46 kg of fossil CO2 and the template 0.222 kg (-84.8 %), 0.0131 kg of methane against 5.7E-5 (-99.6 %), 0.0042 kg of SO2 against 1.2E-4 (-97.2 %), 0.0028 kg of NOx against 1.1E-4 (-95.9 %). A factor 6.6 on CO2 and two orders of magnitude on methane. Overall 1 of 1670 determined flows within +-10 %, 0 of the 50 largest kilogram flows. The two are different answers to the same allocation question - ecoinvent spreads the refinery's burden over the whole product slate, the APME profile charges the aromatics extraction and reforming to the aromatics - and the gap between them is roughly the size of that decision. Practical consequence: this node is a legitimate disaggregation but it is NOT a drop-in replacement, and any chain that terminates on it (ethylbenzene, cumene, and through them the styrene and acetone rebuilds of this same batch) inherits the difference. That is worth more than the score: it says the remaining gap in the BTX family is an allocation decision, not missing data.

replaces.name: Polymethyl methacrylate, beads, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model from the dataset's own process description: monomer by mass balance, utilities from the BAFU chemicals template and calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory for this dataset. The input list comes from the dataset's own ecoSpold technology field, 'production by different types of polymerization out of MMA'. The field names the monomer outright; 'beads' is the suspension-polymerised form. Chain-growth (addition) polymerisation: the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula, so 1 kg of polymer carries 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No conversion-loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the true value can only be higher - fixed, not fitted. Same convention as the committed HDPE / LDPE / LLDPE / PP / PVC specs. The monomer is itself an unflagged PlasticsEurope eco-profile (results/system_terminated_extended.csv, detected_by=structure), so this model terminates on an aggregated dataset and the structural check says so - correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

evidence.note: quoted in the strategy note; it is the structural evidence for the input list

evidence.note: specs/evidence/cde75755-0bae-3223-89c8-c38412981461/response-0-locate.json - no report in the BAFU-2026 documentation bundle prints a unit-process inventory for this dataset. replaces.name: Acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene copolymer, ABS, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the three monomers the dataset names, split fitted under a 1 kg mass constraint, utilities calibrated
strategy.note:
NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field - 'production by emulsion polymerization out of its three monomers' - states the number of monomers, and the product name states which three: acrylonitrile, butadiene and styrene. That is the structure. No composition is printed anywhere in the bundle (the 2025 plastics report lists the 2015 PlasticsEurope ABS eco-profile in Tab. 6.1 and prints no inventory for it), so all three are free under mass_sum = 1.0 kg and the split is a fit, not a measurement - flagged low confidence. Two of the three monomers are themselves unflagged eco-profiles, so this model terminates on aggregated data and the structural check says so.

AFTER THE FIT - READ THIS BEFORE USING THE AMOUNTS. The calibration was run and its result is structurally wrong, which is worth more than the spec was: the fit drove acrylonitrile - the monomer the product is named after - to 8.9E-10 kg, i.e. zero, and split the kilogram as 0.601 kg butadiene / 0.391 kg styrene, where a real ABS is roughly 20 % acrylonitrile, 20 % butadiene and 60 % styrene. The inventory agreement it buys is the best in the whole family: 1221 of 1667 determined flows within +-10 % (73 %), median |delta| 6.7 %. This is the identifiability trap the project's own calibration benchmark predicts (README sec. 6: 'a better inventory fit with the wrong structure'), caught here on real data rather than on a synthetic case. The mechanism is specific and repeatable: under a mass constraint, when one candidate monomer is another dataset of the same APME eco-profile family and another is an ecoinvent unit process, the fit will empty the ecoinvent one, because it drags in a full background of ~1670 elementary flows that the target's ~145-substance eco-profile simply does not have, and every one of them counts against the fit. And among same-family candidates the fit follows the waste-treatment exchanges, not the chemistry - which is why it prefers polybutadiene to styrene: 'Styrene, at plant' declares 0.5615 kg of hazardous waste to incineration per kg, 80x what its own polymer GPPS declares (0.0070 kg) and 250x its own feedstock benzene (0.0022 kg), so any node that links styrene inherits a waste chain the target does not have. Conclusion for a user: the node's *inventory* is a fair reconstruction of the target's flows, its *composition* is not a statement about the product, and the split must not be quoted. The amounts are left exactly as the fit produced them - no bound was moved after the score was seen.

replaces.name: Polyethylene, LLDPE, granulate, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: monomer by mass balance, input list from the dataset's own process description, energy calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. The cited report prints no inventory. The input list is the one the BAFU dataset itself declares in its ecoSpold technology/includedProcesses field, and the monomer amount is a mass balance, not a measurement: addition (chain-growth) polymerisation adds the monomer to the chain unchanged, so the repeat unit and the monomer have the same empirical formula and 1 kg of polymer needs 1 kg of monomer plus whatever is lost. No loss figure exists anywhere in the bundle, so 1.000 kg is used and the real value can only be higher - this is the one place where the model is knowingly at a bound. Electricity and steam are named by the dataset and quantified nowhere, so they are fitted, unbounded; they are the whole gate-to-gate difference between the polymer and its monomer. The alpha-olefin comonomer (typically a few per cent of 1-butene or 1-hexene) is a gap: no comonomer is named in the dataset's own text and no dataset for one is identified, so it is carried inside the ethylene.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf (the dataset's own cited report)
evidence.note: Prints no unit-process inventory for any of its 14 datasets: 'All datasets addressed for the updates are nowadays only available as system processes and therefore are modelled accordingly in this study' (sec. 3.2); Foreground data = 'Cumulative inventories of Plastics as provided by PlasticsEurope' (Tab. 1.1). Verified page by page, including every table that is embedded as an image. The full finding is in specs/evidence/<code>/response-0-locate.json. What the report does give and is used here: sec. 3.6 (infrastructure, 4.0E-10 p of Chemical plant, organics).

evidence.source: bafu-2026 ecoSpold metadata of the target (includedProcesses / technology)
evidence.note: 'The polymer process, upstream processes like ethylene production, electricity, and steam production as well as transportation of feedstock and waste treatment.' - the whole input list the dataset declares.

evidence.source: 2025 - LCI plastics - Rajabihamedani.pdf
evidence.where: Tab. 5.3 (cross-check only, not used for any amount)
evidence.note: Cumulative energy demand, this study: LLDPE 76.95 MJ/kg against Ethylene, average 70.73 MJ/kg - about 6.2 MJ/kg, 8 % of the total. Quoted as a sanity check on the fitted electricity and steam, and deliberately not used to set or bound them: it is an impact result, and no impact assessment enters this pipeline.

nodes.name: Polyethylene, LLDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Polyethylene, LLDPE, granulate, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: Polymerisation step, per kg of granulate. The waste-treatment services that the BAFU dataset already carries as explicit exchanges (Tab. 3.1 of Rajabihamedani 2025 documents how they were re-linked, but prints no amounts) are deliberately NOT part of this model: they were never collapsed away, so reconstructing them adds nothing, and copying their amounts out of the target would be reading the answer. Adding the whole Tab. 3.1 candidate list as free inputs was tested on Ethylene glycol - the fit drove all eleven to ~1e-12 and the agreement did not move by a single flow - so they are left out. Consequence for the harness number: the target's cumulative vector gets its long tail of trace flows from those disposal chains, while this model gets a different tail from the ecoinvent-v2 chains of its own inputs; the two tails cannot agree, which caps the 'share of all flows within 10 %' far below what the main flows achieve. This model terminates on Ethylene, average, at plant [RER], which is itself an ecoSpold type=2 dataset - the harness flags that, correctly. It is linked to the BAFU dataset rather than to the sibling rebuild so that this spec's check measures only this spec's evidence; re-point it with the input's `sandbox` field to chain the rebuilds together.

technosphere.comment: Rajabihamedani 2025 sec. 3.6: 'For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The target carries exactly that, which is why 4.0E-10 is the upper bound here. It is the upper bound and not the amount because ESU added one chemical plant per *dataset*, i.e. one for a whole cradle-to-gate chain, while this model links to a precursor dataset that already carries its own 4.0E-10 - so a second one is a double count against the target's own convention. That matters more than its size suggests: of the 1790 flows in the cumulative vector of every one of these 14 datasets, 1316 get more than 90 % of their value from this single exchange (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py), so doubling it doubles three quarters of the vector. The amount is therefore fitted between 0 and the report's 4.0E-10.

The dataset's own text names 'transportation of feedstock' but no report in the bundle gives a distance for it, so the amount is calibrated. The starting value is the ecoinvent v2 standard distance for precursor materials (Althaus 2007 sec. 34.6.7: 'As there is no information about the transport amounts, standard distances and means according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used for the different raw materials') = 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor, the ratio BAFU's Ethylene dichloride, Ethylene oxide, Ethyl benzene and PET-amorphous unit processes all carry; precursor mass here 1 kg. It is left free rather than fixed because the PlasticsEurope eco-profile accounts for its feedstock transport as elementary flows only - it carries no vehicle or track infrastructure - so an ecoinvent transport dataset adds a background the target cannot have, and the fit is the right place to decide how much of it belongs.

strategy.note: basis: the chromic acid column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000' - i.e. per 3000 kg of anthraquinone; allocation: none stated; 3 of 9 inputs carry a printed amount, 4 a printed range, 2 no number in the report (xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid, Chemical plant, organics). evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 6d1899c288e051fa…

gaps_reported_by_model: The dataset is an 80/20 average: 'an average process from the chromic acid process in Tab. 44.3 and the information at EMPA from the former studies is established - with an amount of 80% chromic acid process'. Only the chromic acid column is printed; 'the respective information from EMPA is not shown here due to confidentiality reasons'. The extracted list is therefore the 80 % share only.

The EMPA share contributes chlorobenzene (modelled as benzene + chlorine at 95 % yield) and aluminium chloride (modelled as aluminium + chlorine at 95 % yield). No amounts are given, so those four inputs are NOT included here.
The sulphuric acid amount actually used is 'the stoechiometric value based on an efficiency of 95%', which the report does not print.
Electricity, steam, infrastructure and both transports are named by the report but carry no numbers; they are free parameters for calibration.
The air emissions are given as percentage rules applied to inputs the report itself replaces, so their absolute values are uncertain.
'Due to confidentiality reasons, only the cumulated data from this dataset are available for the user of ...' - the dataset's own unit-process table is not published.
skipped_items: air (flow rate): ignore — Explicitly excluded by the report: 'The amount of air consumed is not shown in the ecoinvent dataset according to Frischknecht et al. (2007).' It is also a flow rate, not an amount per batch.

Sulphuric acid to air: no flow chosen (No candidate is airborne sulphuric acid or a sulfate aerosol. Sulfur Dioxide would be a different substance with a different formation route, and mapping sulphuric acid mist onto SO2 would be a substitution the report does not make. Reported as missing instead.)

naphthalene: ignore — Belongs to the naphthalene route, marked only with 'x' (no quantity). The report says 'this second source allows no quantification of the process in three of the four cases' and builds the dataset from the chromic acid column only.
xylene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
butadiene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
anthraquinone: product — Reference product; fixes the basis at 3000 kg.

replaces.name: xx Nylon 6, glass-filled, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: the two components the dataset's name and technology field state, split fitted under a 1 kg mass constraint
strategy.note:
NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field states the composition qualitatively - 'production by different ways out of caprolactam and filled with glass fibers' - and both components exist in BAFU: the unfilled polymer as an unflagged eco-profile and 'Glass fibre, at plant' [RER] as a real 20-input unit process. Compounding is a physical blend, so polymer + glass = 1.000 kg per kg of compound, which is imposed with mass_sum; the glass content is nowhere quantified in the bundle (commercial grades run 15-50 %), so the split is fitted, not measured, and is flagged low confidence. Note the circularity BAFU already contains and this spec inherits: 'Glass fibre, at plant' itself consumes 0.0283 kg of 'Nylon 6, at plant' as a sizing agent, so a glass-filled nylon depends on nylon twice.

AFTER THE FIT - READ THIS BEFORE USING THE AMOUNTS. The fit put 0.99999 kg on the polymer and 4E-6 kg on the glass fibre, i.e. it modelled a glass-*filled* compound as unfilled polymer; commercial grades carry 15-50 % glass. The inventory agreement it buys is real (429 of 1668 determined flows within +-10 % (26 %), 85 % of the kilogram mass, median |delta| 19.9 %) and the node is a fair reconstruction of the target's flows, but its composition is not a statement about the product and must not be quoted. The mechanism is the same one recorded on the ABS, SAN and HIPS specs: under a mass constraint the fit empties whichever candidate is an ecoinvent unit process - here 'Glass fibre, at plant', a 20-input dataset that drags a full ~1670-flow background into a target whose eco-profile reports ~145 substances - and keeps the candidate that belongs to the same APME family and therefore shares the target's waste-treatment chains. No bound was moved after the score was seen.

replaces.name: Polyols, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: top-down model: propylene oxide by the alkoxylation mass balance, utilities calibrated
strategy.note: NOT S1. No report in the bundle prints an inventory. The dataset's ecoSpold technology field is 'production out of alcohols and epoxides by alkoxylation'. Alkoxylation is an addition: the epoxide opens onto the growing chain with no mass loss, so epoxide + initiator alcohol = 1.000 kg per kg of polyol. The epoxide of a polyether polyol is propylene oxide (with some ethylene oxide in tipped grades), and BAFU carries 'Propylene oxide, liquid, at plant' as a real 8-input unit process. The initiator alcohol cannot be modelled: it is glycerol, sucrose or a glycol depending on the grade, the field does not say which, and BAFU-2026 has no petrochemical glycerol dataset at all - the only glycerine datasets in it are biodiesel co-products from rape and vegetable oil, which would import an agricultural background that has nothing to do with this product, and one deprecated 'xx Glycerine, from epichlorohydrin'. So the whole 1.000 kg is charged to propylene oxide, and unlike every other stoichiometric amount in this batch that is an UPPER bound, not a lower one: the true propylene-oxide content is 1.000 kg minus the initiator, typically a few to ten per cent. It is fixed rather than fitted because there is no printed range to bound it with. The ethylene-oxide tip of the common grades is a second, unquantifiable gap.

strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of TiO2; Tab. 85.3 'Kg per kg of product', Tab. 85.4 'Consumption per kg of product (MJ/kg)', Tab. 85.6 and Tab. 85.8 'Gram per kg of product'. The SULFATE-process column is used.; allocation: none stated; the report notes filter salts 'that are produced can be sold' but gives no allocation; 2 of 7 inputs carry a printed amount, 5 a printed range, 0 no number in the report. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 e1b3f9c29c3269b8…

gaps_reported_by_model: Section 85.6: 'This inventory is based on confidential information provided by industry sources. The input information may not be divulged.' The BAT-Notes tables are what the report prints; the dataset's exact amounts are not published.
No transport, no chemical-plant infrastructure and no process-water input are quantified in the excerpt.
The report mentions that gypsum can be generated if the acid is neutralised with lime and that filter salts can be sold, but gives no amounts and no allocation, so neither is included.
Several air-emission rows (NOx, H2S) are printed only as ranges with no value marked as used; their midpoints are used and flagged low confidence.

replaces.name: Acetone, liquid, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1000 kg of acetone, the basis of the only quantitative statement in the chapter (sec. 1.5.2, citing Wells 1999); allocation: None. Acetone and phenol are co-products of the cumene process - 'Acetone and phenol are co-products and their production and demand are intertwined' - and the excerpt states that the cumene figure excludes the phenol ('The production of the co-product phenol is not included in this figure'), i.e. 100 % of the cumene is charged to the acetone. No burden is shifted to phenol here either.; 1 of 1 inputs carry a printed amount, 0 a printed range, 0 no number in the report. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 3d1e65fc1ab8cd34…

gaps_reported_by_model: Sulphuric acid for the cleavage step: named in the excerpt, never quantified.
Electricity and process heat: the chapter gives reaction conditions (200-250 C and 15-35 bar for the alkylation, 300-450 C and 2-3 bar for the isopropanol route) but no energy figure at all.
Direct emissions: the chapter prints none for the unit process; Tab. 3.2 and Tab. 3.3 are the cumulated vector of the target itself and are deliberately outside the excerpt.
Catalyst, infrastructure and feedstock transport: not mentioned.
The distillation losses and the neutralisation of the residual acid are described qualitatively only.

The route split: the chapter names a second route (dehydrogenation of isopropyl alcohol, 90-95 % yield) and then says the PlasticsEurope data 'assumes that acetone stems from the oxidation of cumene, i.e. the isopropyl alcohol production route is not included in this inventory', so the cumene route is the right one - but no share is given for reality.
skipped_items: Phenol: co-product — Stoichiometric co-product of the same cleavage: 94.11/58.08 = 1.62 kg of phenol per kg of acetone. Recorded for completeness only - the excerpt gives no allocation and explicitly excludes phenol from the cumene figure, so no credit is taken and the whole burden stays with the acetone. (kind = co-product, so it is skipped by the assembler.)
Sulphuric acid: ignore — Named by the excerpt as the cleavage catalyst but never quantified, so per rule 8 it cannot carry an amount; recorded as ignore and repeated in gaps.
Oxygen / air: ignore — Air oxidation; the excerpt gives the equation but no air or oxygen amount, and ecoinvent does not inventory air.

nodes.name: Acetone, liquid, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Acetone, liquid, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 98-99

technosphere.comment: The only number in the whole chapter that belongs to the unit process rather than to the cumulated vector. It is internally consistent: the cumene cleavage is C6H5C(CH3)2OOH -> C6H5OH + CH3COCH3, so 1 kg of acetone (M = 58.08 g/mol) carries 120.19/58.08 = 2.07 kg of cumene at full conversion, and 2.07/0.90 = 2.30 kg at the 90 % yield the sentence states - exactly the printed 2300 kg per 1000 kg. The figure therefore assigns the whole cumene input to the acetone and none of it to the phenol, which is what the second sentence says.

provenance.quote: Wells (1999) indicates that 2300 kg of cumene are required to produce 1000 kg of acetone with a yield of 90%. The production of the co-product phenol is not included in this figure.
provenance.mapping_reason: The only candidate that is the substance at all - the other seven are a pulp plant, an anode plant, a silicone plant, soap, brick, latex and a magnesium plant, none of which is cumene. It is a 7-input unit process, not an aggregated dataset, so the chain terminates properly here; its own inputs (0.684 kg benzene + 0.369 kg propylene) are the alkylation the excerpt describes.

replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: transcribed cumene requirement, mass-allocated between acetone and its phenol co-product, utilities from the BAFU chemicals template and calibrated
strategy.note: Labelled S3, not S1, although the cumene figure is a straight transcription - because the number that goes into the node is not the number the report prints, and that difference is the point of this spec. Chapter 3 of 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf, sec. 1.5.2, states: 'Wells (1999) indicates that 2300 kg of cumene are required to produce 1000 kg of acetone with a yield of 90%. The production of the co-product phenol is not included in this figure.' Those 2300 kg are the *unallocated* requirement - 120.19/58.08 = 2.07 kg of cumene per kg of acetone at full conversion, divided by the stated 90 % yield, is 2.30 kg exactly - so charging them all to the acetone gives the phenol a free ride, and the phenol is the heavier product of the two (1.62 kg per kg of acetone). This spec therefore applies mass allocation: Cumene cleavage: C6H5C(CH3)2OOH -> C6H5OH + CH3COCH3, i.e. one phenol (94.113) per acetone (58.080), so the printed 2.300 kg of cumene per kg of acetone produces 1.620 kg of phenol alongside it. Mass allocation between the two co-products gives acetone 58.080/(58.080+94.113) = 38.16 % of the cumene, i.e. 2.300 x 0.38162 = 0.87772 kg per kg of acetone. Both numbers in that product are printed: 2300 kg per 1000 kg is Wells (1999) as quoted by Althaus sec. 1.5.2, and the molar masses are standard. Molar masses from the IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Na 22.990. A companion spec, specs/f44d9ac3-acetone-liquid-at-plant.draft.json, is the unallocated transcription produced by the LLM route, and the two are meant to be read together. Disclosure, because it matters for how much weight the agreement figures deserve: the unallocated spec was built and checked first, and its flow diff showed its cumulative fossil CO2 at 4.06 kg against the target's 1.79 kg, a factor 2.3 - which is what prompted writing the allocated variant. The allocation is a modelling decision argued from the reaction equation and stated here in full, not a bound tuned until the score improved; no amount in this spec is free except the utilities, which carry no allocation question. Known gaps: the sulphuric acid of the cleavage step, named by the chapter and never quantified; the oxygen/air of the oxidation; and the second route the chapter describes (dehydrogenation of isopropanol), which the chapter says the PlasticsEurope data does not include.
